nodes.label: Never Do These
nodes.rationale: The hard prohibitions: push straight to main, commit secrets, commit real buyer data, force-push a shared branch, and bypass the checks.

nodes.label: Working With AI Coding Agents
nodes.rationale: AI agents are welcome, but the human owns everything they write.

nodes.label: Checklist
nodes.rationale: The closing self-check: one thing and no and in the title; bun run check and bun run format run and CI green; open pull requests checked for overlapping files and related issues linked; the last commit refreshes the Graphify graph; the whole diff read including anything an AI agent wrote; UI follows docs/DESIGN.md with no browser-native inputs or selects; docs updated if behaviour changed; no secrets, .env files or real buyer data.

nodes.label: Follow The Design Guide And Shared UI Components
nodes.norm_label: follow the design guide and shared ui components
nodes.rationale: UI must follow docs/DESIGN.md and use the components in frontend/src/components/ui/, never browser-native inputs, selects or date pickers, so Mortar stays visually consistent and accessible.

nodes.label: Keep AI Agents On Task
nodes.rationale: Ask for one change at a time, matching one issue; large mixed changes from an agent are the fastest way to a messy repo.

nodes.label: Never Force-Push A Shared Branch
nodes.rationale: Never run git push --force on a branch someone else works on, because it silently destroys their commits.

nodes.label: No Pushes Straight To main
nodes.rationale: Always go through a pull request, because the pull request is the last review before the live site.

nodes.label: Never Commit Real Buyer Data
nodes.rationale: No real names, IC numbers, phone numbers or bank details in code, test data, screenshots or issues; all Mortar data is synthetic. See docs/TRD.md#data-retention.

nodes.label: Never Commit Secrets
nodes.rationale: No .env files, API keys, passwords or tokens. Use .env.example for placeholders only, so a placeholder can never be mistaken for a live credential.

nodes.label: One Problem Per Issue
nodes.rationale: If you find a second problem, open a second issue, so each issue stays small enough to review and close.

nodes.label: One Thing Per Pull Request
nodes.rationale: If the title needs the word and, split it. Aim for under about 400 changed lines, not counting bun.lock, so review and revert stay tractable.

nodes.label: Point Agents At The Rules
nodes.rationale: Agents read AGENTS.md, which links back to this guide, so the written rules reach the agent instead of living only in a human's head.

nodes.label: Read The Diff Before Committing
nodes.rationale: Read every changed line before committing. If you cannot explain a change, do not ship it, because unexplained code becomes unreviewable and unmaintainable code.

nodes.label: Update The Docs In The Same Pull Request
nodes.norm_label: update the docs in the same pull request
nodes.rationale: If behaviour changed, update the PRD, TRD or docs/agents/notes.md in the same pull request, so the docs never drift from the deployed behaviour.

nodes.label: Data Check
nodes.rationale: A required checkbox the reporter must tick confirming the report and screenshots contain no real buyer names, IC numbers, phone numbers or bank details. Because screenshots are encouraged, the form pushes the privacy rule to the exact moment a real name could be pasted or photographed into the issue.

nodes.label: graphify affected
nodes.rationale: Lists what a change to something would touch, for example graphify affected "PERSONA_PAGES".

nodes.label: graphify explain
nodes.rationale: Describes one node and its neighbours, for example graphify explain "nextStepFor".

nodes.label: graphify god-nodes
nodes.rationale: Reports the most connected nodes, i.e. the hubs a reader should be careful around when changing something.

nodes.label: graphify path
nodes.rationale: Finds how two things connect, for example graphify path "AskPanel" "createAssistant".

nodes.label: graphify query
nodes.rationale: Walks the graph breadth first and answers a question in words, for example graphify query "how does Today choose each card's next step". Add --dfs to trace one path and --budget N to cap the answer at N tokens, so a search that would otherwise sprawl is bounded.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md is the plain-language overview, for a reader who wants the shape of the repository without running a query.

nodes.label: Ask The Graph First
nodes.rationale: Before searching with grep or opening file after file, query the graph. Fall back to grep only when the graph does not answer, or when exact text or line numbers are needed, because those are the two cases a graph cannot serve.

nodes.label: Graph First, Then Grep
nodes.rationale: Have agents query the Graphify graph (graphify query) before grepping; it answers most questions for far fewer tokens.

nodes.label: What You Expected
nodes.rationale: Required textarea: what should have happened instead, which separates a genuine defect from intended behaviour.

nodes.label: Steps To Reproduce
nodes.rationale: Required textarea asking for the exact steps someone else can follow, with a worked example placeholder (sign in as Sales Admin, open Today, click the first card, see the error) because a bug another person can reproduce is a bug that can be verified and regression-tested.

nodes.label: What Happened
nodes.rationale: Required textarea: what went wrong, including any error message word for word, so the developer can search logs for the exact text.

nodes.label: Where: Live Site / Running Locally / Both
nodes.norm_label: where: live site / running locally / both
nodes.rationale: Required dropdown separating deployed-only faults from local-only faults, which points straight at whether the deploy or the dev environment is at fault.

nodes.label: Pitch Priority
nodes.rationale: Required dropdown asking how much the request matters for the Chin Hin pitch, with options Blocks the pitch, Improves the pitch, After the pitch. It ties ordering to an external deadline rather than to whoever filed first.

nodes.label: How To Check It
nodes.rationale: Numbered steps a reviewer can follow, with a worked example (sign in as Sales Admin, open Today, click the first card), so verification is written down next to the change and can be repeated on the live site after the deploy.

nodes.label: Branch Naming Convention <type>/<short-topic>
nodes.rationale: Lowercase with hyphens, prefixed by one of five types: feat (new capability), fix (something broken), ui (look and layout only, no behaviour change), docs (documents only), chore (tooling, dependencies, config, cleanup). Example: feat/chase-quick-confirm.

nodes.label: Commit Message Format type(scope): what changed
nodes.norm_label: commit message format type(scope): what changed
nodes.rationale: Lowercase and imperative, like an instruction. Type is the same list as branch types; scope is optional and names the area touched, such as chase, import, legal, forecast, landing or survey.

nodes.label: The Journey Of A Change
nodes.rationale: Issue -> Branch -> Commits -> Pull Request -> Review -> Squash Merge -> Live. Each step answers what and why, keeps the branch your own copy, commits in small steps, lets CI check it, needs a teammate approval, lands one commit on main, and confirms the change on the live site.

nodes.label: When Something Breaks On The Live Site
nodes.norm_label: when something breaks on the live site
nodes.rationale: Three steps: tell the team first in chat with a screenshot and page link; revert rather than patch, by clicking Revert on the merged pull request and merging the revert pull request, which restores the last working version within minutes; then fix calmly through a bug issue and a new branch on the normal journey.

nodes.label: Pre-Commit Hook Formats Staged Files
nodes.rationale: The hook formats staged files automatically; if it fails, read the message, fix it and commit again rather than skipping it.

nodes.label: Reviews And Merging
nodes.rationale: The gate between a finished pull request and the live site: one teammate's approval, green checks, every comment answered, squash and merge, branch deleted, live site checked.

nodes.label: Contact Link: How We Ship Changes
nodes.norm_label: contact link: how we ship changes
nodes.rationale: Because blank issues are off, the chooser shows a single link to .github/CONTRIBUTING.md on main with the text Read this before opening your first issue or pull request, so a person who wants to file something unprompted still lands on the rules first.

nodes.label: Type Of Change
nodes.rationale: Checkbox list mirroring the branch and commit types: Feature (a new capability), Fix (something was broken), UI (look and layout only), Docs (documents only), Chore (tooling, dependencies or config).

nodes.label: Answer Every Comment Then Resolve The Thread
nodes.norm_label: answer every comment then resolve the thread
nodes.rationale: Reply or push a fix, then resolve the thread, so no reviewer concern is left silently open at merge time.

nodes.label: Check The Live Site After The Deploy
nodes.norm_label: check the live site after the deploy
nodes.rationale: Open the live site after the deploy finishes and try the change as a real user would, since green CI does not prove the change works in the deployed bundle.

nodes.label: Delete The Branch After Merging
nodes.rationale: Click Delete branch after merging, so the branch list shows only live work and no one branches off an already-merged copy.

nodes.label: Merging Into main Deploys To The Live Site
nodes.norm_label: merging into main deploys to the live site
nodes.rationale: There is no staging step between merging into main and the live site, so a pull request is the last chance to catch a mistake. Everything else in the guide exists to protect that moment.

nodes.label: Green Checks Only
nodes.rationale: Merge only when every check shows a green tick, since merging ships straight to the live site.

nodes.label: Never Merge Your Own Pull Request
nodes.norm_label: never merge your own pull request
nodes.rationale: Wait for one teammate's approval, because a pull request is the last chance to catch a mistake before the live site.

nodes.label: One Branch, One Change
nodes.rationale: Do not reuse a merged branch for new work, so review and revert stay scoped to one change.

nodes.label: Run The Checks Locally Before Pushing
nodes.norm_label: run the checks locally before pushing
nodes.rationale: Run bun run check, then bun run format. CI runs the same checks and blocks the merge if they fail, so running them locally only saves a round trip.

nodes.label: Small Steps, One Working Step Per Commit
nodes.norm_label: small steps, one working step per commit
nodes.rationale: Commit each working step separately, not a whole day in one commit, so a reviewer can follow the change and any single commit can be reverted.

nodes.label: Squash And Merge
nodes.rationale: Always choose Squash and merge so main gets one clean commit per change, and edit the squash title into the commit format, which keeps main readable as the change history.

nodes.label: Graphify
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ holds a knowledge graph of the repository. Code files and documents are nodes, imports, calls and references are edges, related nodes are grouped into communities. Asking the graph costs a fraction of the tokens that reading files through repeated searches costs, so agents ask it first.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore
nodes.rationale: Uses .gitignore syntax and applies on top of .gitignore, so a file is only in the graph if neither list excludes it. When a new kind of generated or binary file appears, add it there.

nodes.label: Installing Graphify
nodes.rationale: Install once with uv tool install graphifyy, or pipx install graphifyy, which provides the graphify command. In Claude Code the /graphify skill wraps the same tool, so there is one underlying tool behind two entry points.

nodes.label: graphify update .
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts changed code with no model and no key, so the code half of the graph is cheap to keep current on every change.

nodes.label: What The Graph Leaves Out
nodes.rationale: The ignore list keeps out files with no extractable knowledge: images, video and audio, PDFs and Office files, fonts, archives and binaries, Python bytecode, data dumps, the precomputed Jev cache (server/fixtures/jev-cache.json), lockfiles, vendored agent tooling and the graph itself. Excluding them keeps the node count an honest measure of what the repository actually says.

nodes.label: --force Flag For Node-Count Regression
nodes.rationale: graphify update refuses to write a graph with fewer nodes, a guard against a partial extraction silently shrinking the graph. After a refactor that genuinely deletes code, pass --force to override the guard deliberately.

nodes.label: When To Do A Full Rebuild
nodes.norm_label: when to do a full rebuild
nodes.rationale: Rebuild the whole graph with /graphify . instead of updating it when .graphifyignore changes, or when graphify query cannot find code that is known to exist. A changed ignore list or a missing node means the incremental state can no longer be trusted, so a full pass is the only way back to a correct graph.

nodes.label: Keep It Current
nodes.rationale: The graph is committed to the repository, so main must always carry a current one; a stale graph is worse than none because agents trust it over reading the code.

nodes.label: Never Merge Graph Files By Hand
nodes.norm_label: never merge graph files by hand
nodes.rationale: When two pull requests both change graphify-out/, take either side, run graphify update . again, and commit the result. The graph is a derived artefact, so it is regenerated rather than merged, which cannot produce a graph that matches neither side.

nodes.label: Refresh The Graph As The Last Commit Of Every Pull Request
nodes.norm_label: refresh the graph as the last commit of every pull request
nodes.rationale: Rebase on main, run graphify update ., and commit graphify-out/. Refreshing inside the pull request keeps main current without an extra commit, which would redeploy the prototype.

nodes.label: /graphify . --update Skill For Changed Documents
nodes.rationale: graphify update . covers code only; when a pull request changes documents, also run the /graphify . --update skill, which re-reads changed documents with the model.

nodes.label: Never Bypass The Checks
nodes.rationale: Do not disable a test, lint rule or hook to make a failure go away; ask for help instead, because a disabled check is invisible protection that never runs again.

nodes.label: Refresh The Graphify Graph Last
nodes.rationale: Make graphify update . the last commit so main always carries a current graph. See docs/agents/graphify.md.

nodes.rationale: Search open and closed issues and pull requests with gh first. Comment on a duplicate instead of opening another, and link any issue that overlaps or conflicts. See docs/agents/github.md.

nodes.label: Start With An Issue

It turns the duplicate-search rule from advice into a form field that cannot be skipped, and gives the exact commands rather than the principle.

nodes.norm_label: describe what you saw, not what you think the cause is
nodes.rationale: Opening note: Thanks for reporting. Plain words are fine. The reporter's guess about the cause is treated as unreliable, so the report is asked for as observation rather than diagnosis.

nodes.label: Blank Issues Disabled

nodes.label: Duplicate And Conflict Check
nodes.rationale: The same required checkbox and gh search prompt as the bug form: search open and closed issues and pull requests and link any that overlap or conflict. Duplicated deliberately so the rule holds whichever form someone reaches for.

nodes.rationale: Opening note: A clear problem makes a better change. Asking for the problem first leaves room for a solution different from the one the reporter had in mind.

nodes.label: Human In The Loop
nodes.rationale: Every AI suggestion stays a proposal until an authorized staff member confirms it, preserving accountability across sales, loan, and legal desks. This is why the Jev extraction can be confident while the case stage still never moves on its own.

nodes.label: Honest Accounting
nodes.rationale: A booking is never counted as cash at face value, so financial planning is not corrupted by unrealized revenue. This drives the exclusion of booking-face-value cash projection and the Value At Risk framing.

nodes.label: Deterministic Stall Detection
nodes.rationale: Stall rules are deterministic thresholds rather than opinion, and they apply to every unsigned non-exited booking with no age ceiling. Gating stall reasons on the 30-day horizon would hide the longest-running failures, which are exactly the ones worth chasing.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Jev Resolution Strategy
nodes.rationale: Live call, exact-hash cache fallback, then a stale latest-subject answer, then neutral unavailable answers. The whole point is that a pitch demo survives a Jev outage or complete network disconnection, so the app must work with no API key at all.

nodes.label: Assistant Read-Only Tool Set
nodes.rationale: The assistant may only read the live snapshot through five tools and may never write, never make credit, loan, or legal decisions, and may only cite bookings a tool actually returned. Grounding beats free-form generation so an answer cannot drift from the ledger.

nodes.label: Synthetic-Only Data Policy
nodes.rationale: Every record is invented, so the prototype holds no personal data under the Personal Data Protection Act and no PDPA duty is triggered. That also constrains the Jev local proxy and Ask Mortar, both of which send data to third-party models and may only ever see synthetic data.

nodes.label: Seven Core Design Decisions
nodes.rationale: Look, status colour, type, density, native controls, modes and icons were settled during design system research and are binding; nothing below reopens them.

nodes.label: Flat Ledger Look
nodes.rationale: Mortar rejects decorative SaaS styling: no frosted glass planes, no gradient card fills, no floating drop shadows on data tables, no neon glow blobs. A card is separated from the page by its shadow, never by a coloured edge strip or a grey page band.

nodes.label: Ink Is The Action Colour
nodes.rationale: The application carries no chromatic accent; ink carries --primary, --link and --ring so a grey ramp only distinguishes states. Colour appears solely in the six status tones.

nodes.label: Geist Mono
nodes.rationale: Geist Mono is reserved for unit codes, booking reference numbers and tabular data so machine identifiers are visually distinct from prose.

nodes.label: Tabular Numerals
nodes.rationale: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is required for figures, money and age counters so columns of numbers align and can be scanned.

nodes.label: Colour
nodes.rationale: Components consume semantic tokens defined in CSS custom properties and never write raw hex values; the primitives collection carries 18 calibrated neutrals and no chromatic family.

nodes.label: Six Status Tones
nodes.rationale: The six tones are six bespoke desaturated fg/bg/solid pairs tuned per mode for their own fill and text roles, deliberately not drawn from a Tailwind chromatic family.

nodes.label: Calibrated Contrast
nodes.rationale: The #D8D8D8 hairline is a deliberate step darker than #E5E5E5, whose 1.26:1 fell below the 1.40:1 the earlier hairline carried and lost the ledger structure on a white ground.

nodes.label: Landing Panel Tokens
nodes.rationale: The five hue tokens hold space-separated RGB channels rather than hex so the panel can vary alpha per wash; dark values are pulled down rather than inverted so the panel reads as a lit surface on ink.

nodes.label: Radius Tokens
nodes.rationale: --radius-lg and --radius-xl resolve to 6px so a stray utility class cannot smuggle a larger corner into a desk; 999px pill buttons are banned.

nodes.label: Elevation And Focus
nodes.rationale: The page ground stays white so the shadow is the only thing separating card from page; the hairline softens from --border to --card-border because a full #D8D8D8 line under a shadow reads as a doubled edge.

nodes.label: Icon Supplements A Word, Never Replaces One
nodes.rationale: Icons never carry meaning or status alone and never carry a status tone as their colour; they render in currentColor at the weight of the text beside them. Adding a glyph means adding it to the approved list in the same change.
nodes.norm_label: icon supplements a word, never replaces one

nodes.label: Motion
nodes.rationale: Motion is rapid, functional and purely informative; there are no decorative entrance flourishes.

nodes.label: Status Language
nodes.rationale: Status is conveyed through explicit written language paired with calibrated tones; a colour indicator never appears without its associated word.

nodes.label: Plain Language
nodes.rationale: Mortar is read by sales, loan and legal staff, not engineers. Industry terms stay (SPA, LO, RM, panel bank); the vocabulary of the system that produces the string never reaches the screen.

nodes.label: Jev (assistant)
nodes.rationale: Jev stays because staff refer to it by name, so it is a subject in a sentence rather than a status code; attribution builds trust. What goes is the machine state attached to it.

nodes.label: Name The Thing, Not The Mechanism
nodes.rationale: "Ask buyer for payslip" beats "Request document · Payslip". The user acts on the thing; the record type is ours. Freshness reads as a time, never as a cache state, because a person can act on a time.
nodes.norm_label: name the thing, not the mechanism

nodes.label: Internal Names Stay Internal
nodes.rationale: Component names, token names, table names, model names and pipeline stages never appear in a visible string, tooltip, toast or aria-label. Jev is the one exception because it is a product name the staff already use.

nodes.label: Native Controls Ban
nodes.rationale: Standard HTML browser controls are banned for OS inconsistency, lack of styling hooks and accessibility deficiencies. The single exception: the Drop Zone keeps an sr-only input because a browser cannot open a file picker without one.

nodes.label: One Primary Action Per View
nodes.rationale: A view offers one Primary action, not one Primary button. A queue of "Create Task" buttons is one action offered many times, so every row renders Primary; filling only the first item is forbidden because it reads as a rendering fault.

nodes.label: Day Cell And Date Picker
nodes.rationale: Weeks start on Monday to follow Malaysian business convention.

nodes.label: Stage Tracker
nodes.rationale: No status tone colours a stage bar; the tracker is ink and hairline only, and lapsed or cancelled bookings freeze bars at the last reached stage.

nodes.label: Screen Density
nodes.rationale: An operations screen is a working surface, not a report. One focus per screen, progressive disclosure, chip economy and the tooltip rule keep the ledger readable at a glance.

nodes.label: Public Pages
nodes.rationale: The public pages copy an earlier project, Perch: structure, DOM organization, timings and breakpoints are inherited, but the skin is entirely Mortar tokens and the footer's reveal mechanics were dropped for a static block.

nodes.label: Chromatic Panel (.land-panel)
nodes.rationale: Four radial hue washes plus a centre veil over --land-panel-base; the only gradient and the only chromatic surface in the product, and its padding is what makes the card inside read as inset rather than stacked.

nodes.label: Sample Ledger (illustrative)
nodes.rationale: Its five rows are fixed copy in the component, never fetched, and an sr-only figcaption states they are illustrative so assistive technology hears the disclaimer the sighted reader infers. Do not wire this table to live data.

nodes.label: Landing Type Exceptions
nodes.rationale:
Three steps on the public landing sit outside the nine-style scale and nowhere else may use them. The hero display line takes no width cap because the break is set by hand with an explicit
.

nodes.label: Public Footer
nodes.rationale: The footer closes / and /faq and nothing else. Link column titles are not an Eyebrow because uppercase is reserved for that one style, and not a heading element because an h2 would inject "Product", "Company" and "Code" into the FAQ's question outline.

nodes.label: Sign-In
nodes.rationale: There is no real backend authentication: sign-in presents disabled inputs, a permanently dead Sign In button, a persona selector and a live Sign In As Guest button that writes the persona to localStorage.

nodes.label: bun run check Must Pass
nodes.rationale: ESLint, tsc and Vitest across workspaces must pass before a task is called done; there is no e2e suite, so the check script is the only gate.

nodes.label: @mortar/core Shared Package
nodes.rationale: packages/core resolves straight to src/index.ts, so shared types and logic need no build step or path mapping.

nodes.label: Guided Tour
nodes.rationale: tourSteps.ts selectors must stay aligned with the pages' data-tour anchors and their tests, and its keyboard controls must leave inputs and dialogs usable.

nodes.label: demo_seed Provenance
nodes.rationale: Deletion removes every demo booking with its attached rows, the demo playbooks and the demo meta keys, and touches nothing a visitor created; the provenance marker is what makes that separation possible.

nodes.label: TEST_DATABASE_URL Guard
nodes.rationale: The integration suite reads only TEST_DATABASE_URL and skips when unset, never DATABASE_URL, which often points at production; the team test database is a separate Neon project, mortar-test.

nodes.label: Ask Mortar Gemini Contract
nodes.rationale: Five read-only tools under a 30-second, 4-round budget, messages fenced as untrusted data, and no logging of keys, images or bodies. When GEMINI_API_KEY is unset or a call fails the route returns 503 {fallback:true} and AskPanel falls back to the scripted askBrain answers. The free tier may train on prompts, so Ask Mortar is restricted to simulated data; real buyer data needs a paid tier or Vertex AI under a PDPA agreement.

nodes.label: Imported Bookings Born booked at simNow(REFERENCE_DATE)
nodes.rationale: A sheet row dated after the reference date is refused because the case could not exist yet; ids continue BK-nnnn after the generator's run and stop before the stories' BK-9001.
nodes.norm_label: imported bookings born booked at simnow(reference_date)

nodes.label: nextStep One Next Step Per Case
nodes.rationale: The rule-based move derived from ballInCourt is the default everywhere; a differing cached Jev suggestion only adds an extra 'Jev Suggests: <Step> Instead' line, and Create/Add Task always raises the person-selected step, which avoids duplicate tasks across staff.
nodes.norm_label: nextstep one next step per case

nodes.label: Closed Export (closedExport.ts)
nodes.rationale: buildClosedExportRows stays pure and DOM/network-free so downloadClosedExport can lazy-load write-excel-file/browser, keeping the writer out of every other page's bundle; the export never includes IC or phone.

nodes.label: Jev Runs Without a TypeSafe Key
nodes.rationale: createProxySystemOne adapts a local Anthropic-Messages-compatible proxy such as CLIProxyAPI to the systemOne surface createJevService expects, and server/src/index.ts wires it in when TYPESAFE_API_KEY is unset and JEV_PROXY_URL is set.
nodes.norm_label: jev runs without a typesafe key

nodes.label: JEV_PROXY_MODEL Falls Back On ||
nodes.rationale: .env.example ships the variable empty rather than commented out, and an empty string is falsy, so ?? would let it through and send an empty model name to the proxy.

nodes.label: Persona Pages Drive Sidebar And Route Guard
nodes.rationale: PERSONA_PAGES is the single source of the exact pages visible to each persona and their groups, and PersonaRoute.tsx guards exactly those; the case page, /app, /faq and public pages are never guarded, and switching persona redirects to the new persona's home.
nodes.norm_label: persona pages drive sidebar and route guard

nodes.label: No Data Masking Across Personas
nodes.rationale: PERSONA_PERMISSIONS was removed: nothing in Mortar partitions or hides data per persona, every persona sees identical figures. Persona sets defaults such as preset filters and home views, not data access.

nodes.label: Sidebar Hoists The Persona's Home First
nodes.norm_label: sidebar hoists the persona's home first

nodes.label: Recipe: Add Shared Domain Types Or Logic
nodes.norm_label: recipe: add shared domain types or logic

nodes.label: Both Halves Of /forecast Read One Log
nodes.rationale: forecast() projects forward and leakage() counts backward from the same confirmed events in @mortar/core so what signed and what died cannot drift apart; any recovery estimate must carry its Wilson interval and sample size on screen because the second-bank rate is measured over single-digit resolved cases.
nodes.norm_label: both halves of /forecast read one log

nodes.label: open Is Not live
nodes.rationale: deriveCase computes both; live adds ageDays < HORIZON_DAYS (30) and is what the forecast counts, while open is just unsigned and not exited. Stall reasons derive from open because gating them on live hid every case that had sat longest, the ones most worth chasing; brain.test.ts pins Ask's stalled set to Today's so the two cannot drift apart again.

nodes.label: matchQuestion Ranks On Coverage
nodes.rationale: Keyword score alone does not gate a question because 'What is the weather' out-scores a correct paraphrase, so the score is treated as a floor and ranking uses query coverage; widen tags rather than lowering MIN_COVERAGE.

nodes.label: Focus The Sheet, Not Its First Control
nodes.rationale: A Radix dialog or sheet focuses its first tabbable element on open, which in the quick view was the risk chip and popped its tooltip unasked, running for tens of seconds under jsdom; CaseQuickView focuses the sheet itself in onOpenAutoFocus.
nodes.norm_label: focus the sheet, not its first control

nodes.label: localStorage Access Is Always Wrapped In try/catch
nodes.rationale: Private-mode browsers can throw on localStorage access.
nodes.norm_label: localstorage access is always wrapped in try/catch

nodes.label: Radix Popover Stalls jsdom
nodes.rationale: Radix positions popover content with floating-ui, whose measuring stalls jsdom's event loop for many seconds on every open, holding a setTimeout(0) back 14 to 24s; tests mock @/components/ui/popover with inlinePopover.tsx, which keeps open/close/show-content behaviour and drops positioning while the Calendar stays real.

nodes.label: grid-cols-1 Is Required On Every Responsive Grid
nodes.rationale: A bare grid ... sm:grid-cols-N container has no base column count, so its one implicit column sizes to its widest child's max-content and the page scrolls sideways on a phone.
nodes.norm_label: grid-cols-1 is required on every responsive grid

nodes.label: Radix Popovers Need z-[80] To Clear A Dialog
nodes.rationale: DialogContent sits at z-[71], so a Popover, Select or DropdownMenu that can open while a dialog is open must sit at z-[80] or it renders underneath.
nodes.norm_label: radix popovers need z-[80] to clear a dialog

nodes.label: mock.module Leaks Across A Bun Test Process
nodes.rationale: Bun's mock.module rewrites a module namespace's bindings in place for the whole process, so server/src/__tests__/app.test.ts mocking @mortar/core bled into every later server test file; the server test script now runs src and db as two separate bun test invocations.
nodes.norm_label: mock.module leaks across a bun test process

nodes.label: bun run --filter '*' Fans Out Root Scripts
nodes.norm_label: bun run --filter '*' fans out root scripts
